subject: science
title: US Middle School Science - Electricity and Magnetism
subtitle: Electric charge, circuits, magnetism, electromagnets, motors, generators, and evidence-based explanations.
description: A source-faithful revision pack for middle school physical science. Students review electric charge, static electricity, circuits, current, voltage, resistance, conductors, insulators, magnetism, electromagnets, motors, generators, safety, and evidence-based scientific reasoning.

data.title: Charge Transfer by Rubbing
data.instruction: Put the events in order for a rubbed balloon becoming statically charged.
items: Two neutral objects, such as a balloon and hair, are rubbed together.
Electrons move from one object to the other.
The objects no longer have equal positive and negative charge.
The objects become oppositely charged.
Electric force can make the balloon and hair attract.

data.title: Energy Transfer in a Flashlight
data.instruction: Put the energy transfers in the correct order.
items: Chemical energy is stored in the battery.
The battery provides voltage in a closed circuit.
Current flows through the bulb or LED.
Electrical energy is transferred to the load.
The bulb or LED changes energy into light and thermal energy.

data.title: Building and Testing an Electromagnet
data.instruction: Put the investigation steps in a sensible order.
items: Wrap insulated copper wire around an iron nail.
Connect the wire ends briefly to a battery to make current flow.
Hold the nail near paper clips and count how many are lifted.
Repeat with a different number of wire coils.
Compare the paper clip counts to identify a pattern.
Disconnect the wire between trials so it does not overheat.

data.title: Generating Electricity with Magnetism
data.instruction: Put the generator process in order.
items: Moving water, wind, or steam provides motion energy.
A turbine spins because of that motion.
A magnet and coil move relative to each other.
The magnetic field near the conductor changes.
Electric current is produced by electromagnetic induction.
Electrical energy travels through wires or power lines.
